quote.text: No man is an island, entire of itself; every man is a piece of the continent.
quote.author: John Donne, Devotions upon Emergent Occasions (1624)

stories.headline: An Island Says No to the Continent — and Means It Gently
stories.dek: By 52.8 per cent to 47.2, on a turnout of four in five, Iceland rejected reopening membership talks with the European Union. The margin was 5.6 points; the reason, in the end, was fish. And the prime minister who lost the vote she called it a victory for democracy.

stories.headline: Nvidia Moves to Buy the Town Square
stories.dek: The chipmaker has reportedly agreed to acquire Hugging Face outright for about US$12.9 billion — its largest deal ever, for the neutral hub where the open-model world keeps its weights. A year ago the same company offered to invest, and was turned down.

stories.kicker: The Long Read · The Undercurrent — China
stories.headline: The Huggable Loophole
stories.dek: Beijing spent the summer switching off the AI boyfriend. So the machine grew a plush body — and a generation that will not marry started buying comfort by the handful, three hundred yuan at a time.

stories.headline: The Ceiling Goes Up. The Queue Gets Longer.
stories.dek: For the first time since 2019, the income ceiling for a new HDB flat rises — to S$16,000 for a couple, S$18,000 for an Executive Condo. It lets more households in the door. It does not build a single extra flat.

stories.kicker: The Atelier · Cast Iron & Carbon Steel
stories.headline: The Pan That Outlives You — and the Grail a Machine Stopped Making in 1960
stories.dek: Sand, iron and a fire: the cheapest serious cookware you can buy, and the only kind that gets better the longer you own it. The whole hierarchy is one finishing step — and the money above it buys smoothness, not a better dinner.

stories.kicker: The Home Lab · Running the Big Ones
stories.headline: The Flagship Won't Fit. Its Little Brother Just Became a Daily Driver.
stories.dek: GLM-5.3's 744-billion-parameter flagship is a data-centre object — about 445GB even at four-bit. The genuinely new thing on a dual-5090 rig this week is not a model but the engine stack that finally makes a 300-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts run at home.

stories.headline: A Cinema on Your Nose, Tuned by a Stereo Company
stories.dek: RayNeo's new GT glasses put a claimed 307-inch virtual screen in front of your eyes, with Bang & Olufsen-tuned speakers and, it says, the first Dolby Vision in eyewear — the GT Max at US$399, on sale 4 September. For a sci-fi reader who loves good sound, it is a lot of spec per dollar.

stories.headline: A Watch Dial Made of Clay, and Thrown Away Nine Times in Ten
stories.dek: anOrdain, a Glasgow workshop better known for fired enamel, has put a true porcelain dial on its Model 1 — formed, fired and glazed in-house, at a rejection rate near 90 per cent. From £2,200, and, unusually, no waiting list.

stories.headline: Ridley Scott, Jacob Elordi, the End of the World — and an US$8 Million Weekend
stories.dek: "The Dog Stars," a prestige post-apocalyptic drama from a legendary director and a hot young lead, opened fifth and rotten. Beautifully shot, the reviews agree, is the polite epitaph for a survival film with nothing new to survive.

stories.headline: Puberty Is Arriving Earlier. The Advice Is to Guard the Conversation, Not the Calendar.
stories.dek: Across birth cohorts, the average age of a girl's first period has fallen from 12.5 to 11.9 years, and the share starting before eleven has nearly doubled. Newer work links earlier timing to a modest mental-health tail — which is a reason to talk sooner, not to panic. General guidance, not medical advice.

stories.headline: Gold Rises. The Dollar Rises. That Is the Whole Story.
stories.dek: In a normal week a firmer dollar pushes gold down. This week they climbed together — and that broken link is the tell: a higher-for-longer rate regime running alongside a live debasement trade. Analysis, not advice.

stories.headline: The Bar in Your Kitchen
stories.dek: The gap between a sad home drink and a great bar drink is not a secret ingredient. It is technique, temperature, dilution and ice — and once you feel that, the floor opens under you. Welcome to the home cocktail bar.

stories.headline: Your Grip Is Telling On You
stories.dek: A new cohort study finds the strongest women outlived the weakest by a third — and the link held even for those who never met the aerobic guidelines. Strength is its own longevity lever. General guidance, not medical advice.

stories.headline: An October That Opens With a Sprint
